note: Rolling plan for cantoresmariani.org. Each day: Simple English Propers (CMAA, Creative Commons) with practice videos and the score PDF; 'sing' lists the propers the schola sings that Sunday; 'focus' is the week's rehearsal goal. Hymns are chosen separately.

days.title: Twenty-Ninth Sunday in Ordinary Time
days.gospel: Matthew 22:15–21 · Repay to Caesar what belongs to Caesar
days.focus: Listen only. Hear this week's propers at Mass and notice where they come.

introit.text: I have called out because you answer me, O God; incline your ear and hear my words; keep me, O Lord, like the apple of your eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings.

offertory.text: I shall meditate upon your commandments which I greatly love; I will extend my hands towards your commandments which I love.

communion.text: O Lord our governor, how admirable is your name in all the earth!

days.title: Thirtieth Sunday in Ordinary Time
days.focus: Begin with the Communion. It is short, and the cantor sings the psalm verses between its repeats.

introit.text: Let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice; seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face for evermore.

offertory.text: Lord, grant me life according to your word, so that I may learn your commandments.

communion.text: We shall rejoice in your salvation; and in the name of the Lord our God shall we place our pride.

music.title: Lætetur cor · Let the hearts of those who seek…
Domine, vivifica me · Lord, grant me life according to your…
Lætabimur · We shall rejoice in your salvation

days.title: All Saints
days.focus: Sing the Communion again. Its text is the Beatitudes from today's Gospel.

introit.text: Let us all rejoice in the Lord as we celebrate this feast day in honor of all the saints; it is a solemnity which causes the Angels to rejoice, and to praise together the Son of God.

offertory.text: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no malicious torment will ever touch them; in the eyes of the unwise, they seem to have died; but they are dwelling in peace, alleluia.

communion.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God; blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God; blessed are those who suffer persecution for the sake of justice, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

days.title: Thirty-Second Sunday in Ordinary Time
days.gospel: Matthew 25:1–13 · The wise and foolish virgins
days.focus: Add the Introit, the chant that opens Mass. Keep the Communion.

introit.text: Let my prayer enter into your presence; incline your ear to my supplication, O Lord.

offertory.text: Guide my footsteps, O Lord, according to your word, so that no iniquity may ever gain the upper hand, O Lord.

communion.text: The five wise virgins took oil in flasks with their lamps; at midnight there was a cry: “Behold, the bridegroom is here; come out to meet Christ the Lord.”

days.title: Thirty-Third Sunday in Ordinary Time
days.gospel: Matthew 25:14–30 · The parable of the talents
days.focus: Add the Offertory. That makes all three propers.

introit.text: The Lord says: “I am pondering thoughts of peace and not of affliction; you shall call upon me, and I will hear you; and I will bring you back from all the lands where you are held captive.”

offertory.text: Out of the depths have I cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my prayer; out of the depths have I cried to you, O Lord.

communion.text: Lord, you delivered five talents unto me; behold, I have gained five more. Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your Lord.

days.title: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
days.gospel: Matthew 25:31–46 · The judgment of the nations
days.focus: All three propers. Christ the King closes the Church's year.

introit.text: The Lamb who has been slain is worthy to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honor; let glory and dominion be his for ever and ever.

offertory.text: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the utmost parts of the earth as your possession.

communion.text: Amen I say to you: in as much as you have done it to one of the least of these, my brethren, you have done it to me. Come, O blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world.

days.title: First Sunday of Advent
days.focus: All three propers. Ad te levavi opens the new liturgical year.

introit.text: Unto you have I lifted up my soul. O my God, I trust in you, let me not be put to shame; do not allow my enemies to laugh at me; for none of those who are awaiting you will be disappointed.

offertory.text: Unto you, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul; O my God, I trust in you, let me not be put to shame; do not allow my enemies to laugh at me; for none of those who are awaiting you will be disappointed.

communion.text: The Lord will bestow his loving kindness, and our land will yield its fruit.
